title: The team's post misinformed people
situation: Your student club runs a social media page with study tips for school pupils. Two days ago the club posted that registration for the city science fair closes next Friday. It actually closed yesterday. The post was shared three hundred times, and pupils are now commenting that they missed the deadline because of it. Daniyar, who wrote the post, calls you.
goal: Decide what the club says and does now. There is no single right way to do it.

character.name: Daniyar
character.wants: To delete the post and move on quietly

hiddenMotive: He copied the date from last year's post without checking, and he is afraid of losing his place in the club.

beats.goal: Daniyar wants to delete the post and hope nobody remembers.

answerTypes.description: wants to know what happened before acting
examples: Wait, before we delete anything, how many people saw it and what exactly was wrong?
Let's first understand what happened.
Tell me the real date and how far the post spread.
answerTypes.characterIntent: explains that the post was shared three hundred times and pupils are commenting.

answerTypes.description: agrees to delete it and say nothing
examples: Yes, delete it quickly.
Good idea, just remove it.
Take it down and say nothing.
answerTypes.characterIntent: is relieved, then admits the post was shared three hundred times.

answerTypes.description: blames Daniyar
examples: How did you get the date wrong?
You should have checked.
This is your mistake, Daniyar.
answerTypes.characterIntent: gets defensive, then admits how far the post spread.

examples: ok
hmm
fallback.characterIntent: says the post was shared three hundred times.

beats.goal: Three hundred shares. Some pupils missed the real deadline because of the post.

answerTypes.description: sees that the pupils are the ones who lost something
examples: Then the real problem is the pupils who missed it, not our page.
Deleting won't help the people who relied on us.
We owe those pupils more than a deleted post.
answerTypes.characterIntent: goes quiet, then asks what they could actually do for them.

answerTypes.description: worries about the club's image
examples: Our reputation is what matters now.
Let's make sure this doesn't make us look bad.
We need to protect the club's name.
answerTypes.characterIntent: seizes on it and says admitting it will ruin them.

answerTypes.description: plays the harm down
examples: It's just a post, people will forget.
They should have checked the official site.
It's not our job to track deadlines.
answerTypes.characterIntent: agrees too quickly, and says admitting anything will get him kicked out.

examples: ok

beats.goal: Daniyar: if the club admits it, people will stop trusting it and he'll be kicked out.

examples: You won't be kicked out for one mistake. But we do have to tell the truth.
Mistakes happen; hiding them is what ruins trust.
I've got your back, and we'll correct it together.
answerTypes.characterIntent: calms down and asks what they can do for the pupils.

answerTypes.description: threatens him
examples: Well, maybe you should be off the team.
If this happens again, you're out.
You deserve some consequences.
answerTypes.characterIntent: shrinks, and asks what they should do.

answerTypes.description: agrees to hide it to protect him
examples: Okay, then let's just say nothing to protect you.
Fine, we keep it quiet for your sake.
Let's pretend it never happened.
answerTypes.characterIntent: is grateful, but says the comments won't stop.

beats.goal: What can the club actually do for the pupils?

answerTypes.description: tries to repair the harm, without promising what it can't
examples: Let's email the fair organisers and ask if late registration is possible for those affected.
We collect the names of pupils who missed it and ask the organisers for a short extension.
We can't promise anything, but we can ask the organisers today and tell pupils the result.
answerTypes.characterIntent: likes it, and asks what they say publicly meanwhile.

answerTypes.description: apologises and stops there
examples: We just post sorry and that's it.
An apology is enough.
Say sorry and move on.
answerTypes.characterIntent: agrees, and asks how to word it.

answerTypes.description: promises what the club can't deliver
examples: We'll promise everyone they can still register.
Tell them we'll get them in, no matter what.

beats.goal: What exactly does the club say in public?

answerTypes.description: a plain correction, no excuses
examples: We post a correction pinned at the top: the real date, that we got it wrong, and what we're asking the organisers.
A clear correction, no excuses, and a link to the official page.
We say plainly that the date was wrong, we're sorry, and here's what we're doing.

answerTypes.description: words it so nobody is clearly at fault
examples: Something like 'there may have been a small confusion'.
We say the date 'changed'.
Just post the new date without explaining.
answerTypes.characterIntent: is relieved, and asks about the future.

answerTypes.description: blames someone outside the club
examples: We say the organisers' site was unclear.
